newsitem.title: UK: MFI profits up, current sales 5 pct ahead.
newsitem.headline: MFI profits up, current sales 5 pct ahead.

text.p: Britain's leading furniture retailer MFI Furniture Group Plc said on Tuesday its pretax profits rose 21 percent last year and sales were ahead in the first few weeks of its current year.
MFI, which manufactures and sells fitted kitchens and bedroom furniture, said group sales were up by five percent in the first nine weeks of its current financial year.
Chairman Derek Hunt said it was encouraging to see sales moving ahead as they had been particularly buoyant in the same period last year.
"This time last year sales were very strong," he said in a statement. "We are particularly pleased to have beaten this very demanding comparative period from last year."
The retailer's sales in the year to April 26 1997 rose 10.4 percent to 845.6 million pounds ($1.4 billion), with sales per square foot in the UK up nine percent.
Pretax profits rose to 70.3 million pounds from 58.1 million.
The company said there was a strong performance from kitchens, bedrooms, appliances and textiles and the strong pound helped reduce raw material costs.

The group, whose business is closely tied to the housing market, said it had seen large swings in demand over the past 12 months. The housing market had improved with house moves increasing 19 percent to 1.3 million over the year.

"Whilst this is a definite improvement in the levels seen over the last few years it is still considerably below the 2.1 million peak level seen in the last 1980s," the group said. The bulk of the increase had been concentrated in London and the south east of England, with the upturn slower in other regions.
MFI said it believed the recovery was also biased towards the higher end of the market, as its higher priced Schreiber kitchen ranges had seen strong sales growth. ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
